SEC-001.title: Super-admin can enter tenant-scoped routes without selecting a tenant
SEC-001.problem: `TenantGuard` allows a SUPER_ADMIN request to continue when `tenantId` is undefined. Many downstream services build Prisma filters such as `{ collegeId: c }`. The Prisma schema does not enable `strictUndefinedChecks`; an undefined field is omitted from the query filter. For a super-admin request without `x-tenant-id`, a tenant-scoped list/report can therefore become a cross-tenant query.
SEC-001.fix: Require an explicit, validated `x-tenant-id` on every tenant-scoped route for SUPER_ADMIN. Separate platform-wide routes from tenant routes. Reject undefined tenant IDs at service boundaries and enable strict undefined handling where supported. Add a regression test for SUPER_ADMIN with no tenant header.

SEC-002.title: Analytics scope is broader than the caller's actual access
SEC-002.problem: `scopeDepartments()` returns `p.departmentIds` for every non-admin role, including ordinary teachers. A teacher's department ID is not equivalent to permission to inspect every student in that department. Some trend and department-breakdown methods do not receive the principal at all, so they return college-wide data to callers with `ANALYTICS_VIEW`.
SEC-002.fix: Scope teacher analytics through `AccessService.studentWhere()` / taught offerings. Scope HOD analytics to HOD departments. Pass the principal to every analytics method and enforce the same scope for all endpoints.

SEC-003.title: HOD placement reports are college-wide
SEC-003.problem: `placementReport(c)` queries job applications and student data by college only. The report includes student identifiers/names, CGPA, company, status, and offer/CTC fields. The report builder receives no principal/dept scope for this report.
SEC-003.fix: Pass the principal into report builders and apply the same department/student scope as the corresponding read APIs. Add tests with two departments and verify HOD exports contain only their scope.

SEC-004.title: HOD leave queue returns every department's leave requests
SEC-004.problem: The leave list filters to the teacher's own requests only when the principal has a teacher ID and does not have `LEAVE_APPROVE`. HODs have `LEAVE_APPROVE`, so their list query is tenant-wide. Review actions later enforce department scope.
SEC-004.fix: Add a department filter for HODs; keep college-wide access for College Admin only.

SEC-005.title: HOD can publish a college-wide notice
SEC-005.problem: The service comment says HODs may only target their own department, but the guard only rejects a different department when `dto.departmentId` is present. An omitted department ID is treated as college-wide. The publish path also permits an HOD when the notice has no department ID.
SEC-005.fix: Require HOD notices to include a department ID and verify it belongs to the HOD. Restrict college-wide publication to College Admin / explicitly authorized roles.

SEC-006.title: College Admin can inspect and retry shared cross-tenant queues
SEC-006.problem: The controller comment says queues are shared across tenants and SUPER_ADMIN only, but the guard explicitly permits `COLLEGE_ADMIN`.
SEC-006.fix: Enforce `p.isSuperAdmin` only, or isolate queues by tenant and authorize retry against the job's tenant.

SEC-007.title: Student can message any teacher in the same department as if that teacher were an HOD
SEC-007.problem: The `hod` check compares the target teacher's department with `p.departmentIds`. Student principals include their own department ID, so any teacher in that department satisfies the HOD condition even when the student is not enrolled in that teacher's offering and the recipient is not an HOD.
SEC-007.fix: Check the target user's actual HOD role and matching department scope. Keep the enrolled-offering check for ordinary teachers.

SEC-008.title: Any document-upload user can reprocess any tenant document
SEC-008.problem: `reprocess()` checks that the document belongs to the tenant, but does not check that the caller uploaded it or is an admin. Visibility is not checked either.
SEC-008.fix: Apply the same uploader/admin authorization used by `remove()` and `updateVisibility()`, and check visibility before allowing reprocessing.

SEC-009.title: Default malware scanner is a no-op
SEC-009.problem: `NoopScanner.isClean()` returns true and is wired as the default `MALWARE_SCANNER`.
SEC-009.fix: Use a real scanner (for example, ClamAV or a managed scanning service) in production. Fail closed if scanning is unavailable. Make the no-op scanner development-only.

SEC-010.title: User role department scopes are not validated as belonging to the tenant
SEC-010.problem: `UsersService.create()` and `assignRoles()` validate role IDs against the tenant but do not validate `departmentIds`. `UserRole.departmentId` is a direct FK to `Department`, not a tenant-aware composite FK.
SEC-010.fix: Validate every department ID with `OwnershipService.assert('department', id, collegeId)` and add tenant-aware composite constraints.

SEC-011.title: WebSocket revocation does not fall back to the database when Redis is down
SEC-011.problem: WebSocket connection handling checks the Redis revocation key. When Redis is unhealthy, `safeExists()` returns false; unlike the HTTP JWT guard, the gateway does not query `AuthSession.revokedAt`.
SEC-011.fix: Share the same revocation-check service used by HTTP authentication, with a database fallback. Revalidate active sessions for long-lived sockets.

SEC-012.title: Email verification can reactivate an inactive account
SEC-012.problem: `verifyEmail()` unconditionally writes `status: ACTIVE` after consuming a valid email token. It does not require the user's current status to be `PENDING_VERIFICATION`.
SEC-012.fix: Use a conditional update where status is `PENDING_VERIFICATION`; reject or preserve `INACTIVE` / `LOCKED` states.

AUTH-001.title: Refresh-token rotation is not atomic
AUTH-001.problem: Two concurrent refresh requests can both read the same active session before either revokes it. Both then call `revokeSession()` and create a new session in the same family; the update count is not checked.
AUTH-001.fix: Perform a conditional `updateMany` with `revokedAt: null` and require exactly one updated row before creating the replacement token, preferably inside a transaction.

AUTH-002.title: One-time token consumption is vulnerable to concurrent reuse
AUTH-002.problem: `consumeToken()` reads `usedAt`, then performs an unconditional update. Two concurrent requests can both pass the read check and both consume the token.
AUTH-002.fix: Use a conditional `updateMany` where `usedAt: null` and `expiresAt > now`; require `count === 1`.

AUTH-003.title: Resend verification cannot be used by an unverified user
AUTH-003.problem: `POST /auth/resend-verification` is protected by the global JWT guard. Users whose email is not verified cannot complete login and therefore cannot obtain the bearer token required by this endpoint. The frontend calls it without an authenticated session.
AUTH-003.fix: Provide a public, throttled resend endpoint that accepts college code + email and returns a non-enumerating response.

AUTH-004.title: Student and teacher creation can skip verification email dispatch
AUTH-004.problem: `UsersService.create()` only calls `sendVerification()` when no transaction client is supplied. Student and teacher creation call it inside a transaction, then commit without sending verification afterward.
AUTH-004.fix: Dispatch verification after the transaction commits, or use an outbox event written in the same transaction and processed asynchronously.

AUTH-005.title: Email delivery can silently be dropped in production
AUTH-005.problem: SMTP is optional in configuration. The email service logs/drops mail when no SMTP transport is configured instead of failing the operation. The example environment leaves `SMTP_URL` empty.
AUTH-005.fix: Require a working mail provider in production configuration and surface delivery failure through an outbox/retry state. Do not report a verification email as sent when it was dropped.

AUTH-006.title: Verification UI asks for a six-digit code, backend issues a long token
AUTH-006.problem: Backend tokens are 32 random bytes encoded as base64url and DTO validation requires a token of at least 20 characters. The frontend asks for a six-digit code.
AUTH-006.fix: Either implement a real six-digit OTP backend flow or change the UI to accept/paste the actual token and stop claiming a six-digit code is sent.

AUTH-007.title: Shared predictable initial passwords are prefilled for new accounts
AUTH-007.problem: The admin UI pre-fills `Student@12345` and `Faculty@12345`. When an initial password is supplied, the backend immediately marks the user ACTIVE and email verified; no forced password change is required.
AUTH-007.fix: Generate one-time random credentials or invite links; force password setup on first login; never prefill shared credentials.

AUTH-008.title: Frontend tenant selection is fixed to one college and cannot log in a super-admin
AUTH-008.problem: The login API always supplies `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLEGE_SHORT_CODE` or the hard-coded fallback `SDIET`. There is no tenant selector. Backend super-admin login requires no college code, but the frontend always supplies one.
AUTH-008.fix: Add a tenant/college selection flow and a platform-admin login path that omits college code.

AUTH-009.title: “Remember me” does not change token persistence
AUTH-009.problem: The checkbox state is not passed into login/token storage. Tokens are stored persistently in localStorage regardless of the checkbox.
AUTH-009.fix: Implement session storage / persistent storage choice, or remove the checkbox.  ## B. Payments and fee accounting

FIN-001.title: Production registers a mock payment gateway when no real gateway exists
FIN-001.problem: The gateway map starts empty and the condition includes `m.size === 0`, so the mock gateway is registered even in production. The repository contains the mock implementation but no real payment-provider implementation. The mock checkout URL uses a `.local` host.
FIN-001.fix: Remove the `m.size === 0` production fallback. Fail startup or disable online checkout in production until a real gateway is configured and tested.

FIN-002.title: Student UI reports payment success immediately after order creation
FIN-002.problem: Backend `startPayment()` creates a PENDING payment and an order. The frontend `onSuccess` handler sets `paymentSuccess(true)` immediately; it does not redirect to a real gateway or verify a successful webhook/settlement.
FIN-002.fix: Keep the state PENDING until a verified provider callback/return flow updates the payment. Poll/refresh payment status and display success only when backend status is SUCCESS.

FIN-003.title: Receipt UI fabricates a verified-success receipt
FIN-003.problem: The receipt template hardcodes `VERIFIED / SUCCESS` and the success message contains a fixed receipt number `REC-2026-9812`. It is not tied to a settled payment's actual receipt number/status.
FIN-003.fix: Generate receipts only from the backend receipt endpoint for SUCCESS payments, using the real receipt number, tenant branding, payment method, and amount.

FIN-004.title: Refunds are marked processed without calling a payment provider
FIN-004.problem: The refund method creates a `Refund` with status `PROCESSED`, updates the payment status, and subtracts the amount from the student's fee ledger. The gateway interface exposes order creation and webhook verification, but no refund operation is called.
FIN-004.fix: Add provider-specific refund support, create a REQUESTED refund first, reconcile provider refund IDs/statuses, and only mark PROCESSED after provider confirmation. Treat manual refunds as a separately authorized manual process.

FIN-005.title: Webhook settlement does not verify the paid amount
FIN-005.problem: The verified webhook object contains payment details, but the service checks gateway reference and success state without comparing the webhook amount/currency to the expected payment amount/currency.
FIN-005.fix: Compare amount in minor units, currency, gateway reference, merchant/order ID, and payment ID before settlement.

FIN-006.title: Concurrent refund requests can over-refund a payment
FIN-006.problem: The total refunded amount is read before the transaction and no row lock or conditional update prevents two requests from both passing the same remaining-balance check.
FIN-006.fix: Lock the payment row or perform an atomic conditional update; add an idempotency key and a database invariant.

FIN-007.title: Reassigning a fee structure creates duplicate student fee rows
FIN-007.problem: `assign()` uses `createMany()` without checking existing student/fee-structure pairs. `StudentFee` has no unique constraint on `(studentId, feeStructureId)`.
FIN-007.fix: Add a unique constraint and use `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` or an upsert/idempotent assignment transaction.

FIN-008.title: Fee structure accepts unchecked program/batch references
FIN-008.problem: Program/batch IDs are stored without the same tenant ownership checks used by other create flows.
FIN-008.fix: Validate program and batch ownership and ensure the batch belongs to the selected program/department.

FIN-009.title: Student fee adapter reads nonexistent amount fields and pays an aggregate against one fee
FIN-009.problem: Backend returns `amountDue` and `amountPaid`; the frontend sums `f.amount` and `f.paidAmount`. It aggregates outstanding across all fee rows but retains only the first fee ID for payment.
FIN-009.fix: Match the backend response contract and present one payable invoice per fee row, or create a backend aggregate-payment endpoint that allocates payment across rows transactionally.

FIN-010.title: Failed/refunded payment states are displayed as PENDING
FIN-010.problem: Every payment status other than SUCCESS is mapped to PENDING.
FIN-010.fix: Preserve the complete backend payment status enum and map each state explicitly.  ## C. Academic data integrity and business workflows

DATA-001.title: Student academic hierarchy is not checked for consistency
DATA-001.problem: Student create/update verifies that department, program, batch, section, and semester each belong to the college, but does not verify that the batch belongs to that program and department, that the semester belongs to that batch, or that the section belongs to that semester.
DATA-001.fix: Validate the full hierarchy in one transaction using relation checks. Consider composite tenant/hierarchy constraints.

DATA-002.title: Batch can combine an unrelated program and department
DATA-002.problem: The service checks that program and department belong to the college but does not verify the program/department relationship (or a program-department offering rule).
DATA-002.fix: Define the allowed program-department relationship and validate it on create/update.

DATA-003.title: Manual offering enrollment does not enforce section membership
DATA-003.status: Confirmed source behavior; intended exceptions need product confirmation
DATA-003.problem: The enrollment path checks tenant ownership but does not require the student to belong to the offering's section/semester.
DATA-003.fix: Enforce section/semester membership unless an explicit cross-section elective override is provided and audited.

DATA-004.title: Campus event update does not validate a replacement club's tenant
DATA-004.problem: Event creation validates `clubId`; event update does not repeat the ownership check when `dto.clubId` changes.
DATA-004.fix: Validate the new club ID on update and validate `endsAt > startsAt` on both create and update.

DATA-005.title: College bootstrap is not atomic
DATA-005.problem: College creation, role synchronization, and first-admin creation are separate operations without one transaction.
DATA-005.fix: Use a transaction for tenant + roles + admin creation, with a reliable post-commit email outbox.

DATA-006.title: Audit logging is incomplete and can fail silently
DATA-006.evidence: `Backend/src/audit/audit.service.ts`; examples of missing audit calls in `Backend/src/timetable/timetable.service.ts`, `Backend/src/placements/placements.service.ts`, `Backend/src/scholarships/scholarships.service.ts`, and `Backend/src/campus/campus.service.ts`
DATA-006.problem: Several sensitive state changes do not create `AuditLog` entries. `AuditService.log()` catches persistence errors rather than failing the protected operation.
DATA-006.fix: Define mandatory audit events per workflow, persist them transactionally, and do not swallow audit failures for high-impact actions.  ## D. Attendance, assignments, exams, timetable, and complaints

ATT-001.title: Attendance date handling uses UTC rather than the college timezone
ATT-001.problem: Attendance day boundaries and frontend default dates use UTC conversion, while the tenant schema has a configurable timezone. Portal logic also hardcodes `Asia/Kolkata`.
ATT-001.fix: Resolve the tenant timezone and use a consistent local calendar-day conversion at the API boundary.

ATT-002.title: Attendance roster defaults every student to PRESENT
ATT-002.problem: Roster mapping defaults missing status to PRESENT and the page initializes roster rows as PRESENT. The roster endpoint is a class roster, not a date/session-specific saved attendance roster.
ATT-002.fix: Load the attendance session for the selected date/period and represent unmarked students as UNMARKED, not PRESENT. Require explicit confirmation for bulk-present marking.

ATT-003.title: Teacher attendance period is hardcoded to LEC_1
ATT-003.problem: `selectedPeriod` is initialized to `LEC_1`, and submit defaults to `LEC_1`; no period selector is wired into the page.
ATT-003.fix: Load the timetable slots for the selected offering/date and let the teacher select the actual slot/period.

ATT-004.title: Student attendance dispute is a generic complaint, not an attendance correction
ATT-004.problem: The student page creates a generic complaint and does not submit a specific `attendanceId`/desired status into the correction workflow. The backend correction request permission is teacher-oriented.
ATT-004.fix: Add a student correction-request endpoint that binds to the student's own attendance record, then route it through teacher recommendation/HOD approval.

ATT-005.title: Shortage report silently caps the student population at 1,000
ATT-005.problem: The service fetches at most 1,000 students before applying the requested pagination.
ATT-005.fix: Apply filtering and pagination in the database query, or process the full result set in bounded batches.

ATT-006.title: Weekly attendance notification key is not an ISO week
ATT-006.problem: The week key is computed by flooring Unix time by seven days, which is anchored to the Unix epoch rather than ISO calendar weeks.
ATT-006.fix: Use a timezone-aware ISO week/year key.

ATT-007.title: Attendance correction duplicate prevention is race-prone
ATT-007.problem: Pending correction count and insert are separate; schema has no unique pending-correction constraint.
ATT-007.fix: Use a transaction/row lock or a partial unique index enforcing one pending correction per attendance row.

ASSIGN-001.title: Student attachment input submits only the filename
ASSIGN-001.problem: File input stores only `file.name`; submit sends a text string such as “Submitted attachment: filename” and an empty `fileKeys` array. No file bytes are uploaded.
ASSIGN-001.fix: Upload the file through the storage endpoint, receive a storage key, and submit that key. Do not represent filename metadata as an uploaded file.

ASSIGN-002.title: Teacher assignment attachment input is inert
ASSIGN-002.problem: The file input has no `onChange`, upload call, or attachment-key state.
ASSIGN-002.fix: Wire file selection to storage upload and include returned keys in assignment creation.

ASSIGN-003.title: Text-only resubmission can clear existing submission attachments
ASSIGN-003.problem: The update path defaults missing `fileKeys` to an empty array rather than preserving existing file keys.
ASSIGN-003.fix: Update `fileKeys` only when the request explicitly includes the property.

ASSIGN-004.title: Teacher “pending grading” count counts all submissions
ASSIGN-004.problem: Frontend uses `_count.submissions` as pending-to-grade count, but that count includes already graded submissions.
ASSIGN-004.fix: Return an explicit ungraded submission count from backend.

ASSIGN-005.title: Missing-submission adapter does not unwrap the backend response
ASSIGN-005.problem: Backend returns an object with `pastDue` and `students`; the frontend normalizer looks for an array, `items`, or `data`.
ASSIGN-005.fix: Match the exact `{ pastDue, students }` response contract.

EXAM-001.title: `upcoming=false` query is converted to true
EXAM-001.problem: `@Type(() => Boolean)` converts the non-empty query string `"false"` to JavaScript `true`.

EXAM-002.title: Exam Controller role has permission but fails offering-manager checks
EXAM-002.problem: EXAM_CONTROLLER receives `EXAM_MANAGE`, but create/cancel paths use `assertManagesOffering()`, which recognizes admins, teachers, and HODs—not the exam-controller role.
EXAM-002.fix: Add explicit exam-controller scope rules or route exam operations through a dedicated exam-management authorization method.

EXAM-003.title: Student exam adapter ignores backend exam status
EXAM-003.problem: The adapter derives status from scheduled date instead of preserving backend `SCHEDULED`, `ONGOING`, `COMPLETED`, or `CANCELLED`.
EXAM-003.fix: Preserve the backend status and map labels only for presentation.

EXAM-004.title: Admit card uses hardcoded program/department/semester
EXAM-004.problem: The template falls back to “Bachelor of Technology (CSE)” and “Semester 6”; the normalized auth profile does not supply the actual program/department.
EXAM-004.fix: Fetch the student's authoritative academic profile and render its actual program, department, batch, semester, and exam session.

EXAM-005.title: Student results adapter presents an invalid GPA/academic session
EXAM-005.problem: It hardcodes academic year/semester fallbacks, calculates SGPA and CGPA from the same result set, and uses the first/last result as strongest/weakest subject. The page also hardcodes “Top 8% of CSE Batch”.
EXAM-005.fix: Use backend-published SGPA/CGPA and real rank data; otherwise display “not available” rather than fabricated values.

TIME-001.title: HOD timetable management is not department-scoped
TIME-001.problem: Timetable create/update/delete/availability paths receive tenant ID and actor ID but do not enforce the HOD's department scope.
TIME-001.fix: Pass the principal and enforce offering/teacher/room department scope for HODs.

TIME-002.title: Timetable reads ignore validity windows
TIME-002.problem: `forSection()` does not filter `validFrom`/`validTo`; `forStudent()` filters `validTo` but omits `validFrom <= today`.
TIME-002.fix: Apply both validity bounds consistently in every timetable read.

TIME-003.title: Timetable conflict check and create are not atomic
TIME-003.problem: Conflict check runs before insert and there is no database exclusion constraint or transaction-level locking.
TIME-003.fix: Serialize schedule writes per teacher/room/section or add database exclusion constraints.

TIME-004.title: Teacher availability windows accept invalid time ranges
TIME-004.problem: Availability DTO validates numeric bounds but does not require end minute to be greater than start minute.
TIME-004.fix: Validate `endMinute > startMinute` and reject overlapping duplicate windows.

COM-001.title: Sensitive complaint priority can be downgraded by the submitter
COM-001.problem: Sensitive text forces the route/handler to college admin, but final priority is `dto.priority ?? routing.priority`, allowing the user-supplied priority to override the classifier's CRITICAL priority.
COM-001.fix: Enforce CRITICAL for sensitive categories after processing user-supplied fields.

COM-002.title: Frontend complaint statuses/priorities do not match backend enums
COM-002.problem: UI sends `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `UNDER_REVIEW`, and `URGENT`; backend uses `INVESTIGATING`, `OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, and `CRITICAL` (among others).
COM-002.fix: Share generated enum contracts or map explicitly at the API boundary.

COM-003.title: RESOLVED is a backend enum but not a valid transition target
COM-003.problem: The workflow intentionally resolves to `AWAITING_FEEDBACK`; no transition permits entering `RESOLVED`, while the frontend offers RESOLVED.
COM-003.fix: Either add the intended transition or remove/map the frontend RESOLVED option to AWAITING_FEEDBACK.

COM-004.title: Teacher is shown a complaint queue they are not authorized to access
COM-004.problem: The page treats TEACHER as staff and loads the staff queue, but TEACHER does not receive `COMPLAINT_MANAGE`. Conversely, accountant/exam-controller/support roles that do have complaint-management permission are not consistently represented in the frontend role mapping.
COM-004.fix: Drive the queue UI from actual permissions, not a hard-coded role list.

COM-005.title: Complaint assignment accepts any active tenant user
COM-005.problem: Assignee lookup checks active user and tenant but not whether the target user has a role/permission suitable for complaint handling or department scope.
COM-005.fix: Require `COMPLAINT_MANAGE` and matching department/handler scope for the target user.

COM-006.title: Complaint location is collected by the frontend but not persisted
COM-006.problem: The UI collects a location field, but the API adapter/backend DTO/model do not accept or store it.
COM-006.fix: Add a validated location field to the DTO/model or remove it from the form.

COM-007.title: Complaint timeline and assignee are synthesized/mapped incorrectly
COM-007.problem: Frontend expects `timeline` and `assignedTo.user`, while backend returns event/assignee shapes differently. The adapter generates generic timeline entries and fallback desk names.
COM-007.fix: Add a dedicated detail endpoint returning event history and map the actual `assignedTo` user shape.  ## E. Scholarships, placements, AI, documents, and analytics integration

SCH-001.title: Student can apply to inactive or expired scholarships by direct ID
SCH-001.problem: The discovery/matches query filters active/open scholarships, but `express()` only checks tenant ownership and does not enforce `isActive` or deadline.
SCH-001.fix: Enforce active/deadline rules inside `express()`, not only in list endpoints.

SCH-002.title: Scholarship decision can jump directly to DISBURSED
SCH-002.problem: Decision accepts APPROVED, REJECTED, or DISBURSED without validating the current application state.
SCH-002.fix: Add explicit application status transitions and audit each decision.

SCH-003.title: Scholarship match response is nested but student adapter expects flat fields
SCH-003.problem: Backend returns `{ scholarship, match }`; frontend reads `s.id`, `s.name`, `s.provider`, and `s.amount` from the wrapper object and uses generic fallbacks.

PLAC-001.title: maxBacklogs is stored but not enforced
PLAC-001.problem: `maxBacklogs` is present in the job model but omitted from matching and application eligibility logic.
PLAC-001.fix: Include backlog count and `maxBacklogs` in matching and enforce it again at application time.

PLAC-002.title: Student placement cards show fabricated CTC and match score
PLAC-002.problem: The adapter defaults missing CTC to `8.5 LPA`, match score to `92`, and supplies generic branches/skills/rounds when the backend does not return those fields.
PLAC-002.fix: Use the recommendations endpoint returning `{ job, match }`; show unavailable fields as unavailable rather than inventing values.

AI-001.title: `searchKnowledge` sends the wrong request contract
AI-001.problem: Frontend sends `{ query, limit }`; backend Ask DTO expects `{ question, ...filters }`. With strict whitelist validation this request is rejected.
AI-001.fix: Send `{ question: query }` and implement `limit` only if the backend supports it.

AI-002.title: Hindi keyword-only retrieval is not supported by the lexical path
AI-002.status: Confirmed limitation; vector path may partially compensate
AI-002.problem: Lexical query tokenization strips non-ASCII characters and the generated tsvector uses the English dictionary.
AI-002.fix: Add language-aware tokenization/full-text indexes and tests for Hindi queries; preserve vector fallback.

AI-003.title: AI observability log rows are fabricated from error summaries
AI-003.problem: The adapter turns recent errors into “agent execution logs” and fills user role/name with generic values rather than actual execution records. The dashboard also uses a 100% success fallback when there are no calls.
AI-003.fix: Expose a real paginated AI-call/tool-execution endpoint and display N/A when there is no sample.

ANA-001.title: Risk adapter does not unwrap backend `{ students }`
ANA-001.problem: Backend returns an object containing `students`; frontend normalizer looks for an array, `items`, or `data`.
ANA-001.fix: Read `raw.students` and map the nested student/overall structure.

ANA-002.title: Teacher at-risk cards read the wrong fields
ANA-002.problem: Backend returns student identity under top-level `user` and attendance percentage under `overall.percentage`; frontend reads `student`, `name`, `percentage`, or `attendance`.

ANA-003.title: Admin department filter does not filter the dashboard
ANA-003.problem: `deptFilter` is stored and displayed but is not applied to query parameters or chart data.
ANA-003.fix: Include the selected department in query keys/API calls and filter every relevant series.

ANA-004.title: Admin/HOD dashboard contains metrics that are always empty
ANA-004.problem: The adapter fills enrollment trend, CGPA distribution, placement stats, faculty workload, and subject pass-rate arrays with empty defaults because corresponding backend data is not returned by the called endpoints.
ANA-004.fix: Implement backend aggregates or remove unsupported metrics from the UI until available.

DOC-001.title: Document reprocess authorization is missing
DOC-001.problem: See SEC-008. Reprocessing lacks uploader/admin and visibility checks.
DOC-001.fix: Enforce ownership and visibility before enqueueing.

DOC-002.title: Document page defaults to an unsupported document type
DOC-002.problem: Frontend default `POLICY` and several UI types are not in backend `DocumentType` (`REGULATION`, `ATTENDANCE_POLICY`, `EXAM_RULES`, etc.).
DOC-002.fix: Generate frontend enums from backend OpenAPI/schema or map UI labels to valid backend values.

DOC-003.title: Document visibility enum values do not match backend

DOC-004.title: Role-restricted document upload uses the wrong multipart field name
DOC-004.fix: Append repeated `allowedRoleKeys` fields or normalize the bracketed field name in the upload controller.

DOC-005.title: Document processing can remain stuck after queue failure
DOC-005.status: Confirmed source behavior; deployment impact conditional
DOC-005.problem: Upload catches queue failure but leaves the document in UPLOADED state without synchronous fallback. Reprocess returns a queued-style response even if queue insertion fails.
DOC-005.fix: Persist an outbox job, retry enqueueing, or process synchronously in an explicit degraded mode. Return a truthful failure state.

DOC-006.title: Storage attachment keys have no download endpoint
DOC-006.problem: Storage controller exposes attachment upload but no authenticated download/read route for those keys. Documents have their own download route, but general assignment/notice attachments do not.
DOC-006.fix: Add a tenant- and owner-authorized download endpoint that resolves storage keys without exposing raw paths.

DOC-007.title: Default document visibility can hide an uploaded document from its uploader
DOC-007.status: Confirmed default behavior; UI may override it
DOC-007.problem: Backend defaults omitted visibility to ADMIN_ONLY; document list visibility filtering does not automatically grant uploader access to ADMIN_ONLY documents.
DOC-007.fix: Either default to a safe but uploader-visible visibility or explicitly grant uploader access.  ## F. Frontend role and contract coverage

FE-ROLE-001.title: Unsupported backend roles map to STUDENT
FE-ROLE-001.problem: Frontend role normalization does not model all backend roles such as PARENT, EXAM_CONTROLLER, SUPPORT_STAFF, and LIBRARY_STAFF. Unknown roles fall back to STUDENT. It also selects a single role from the returned role list, which can hide secondary roles.
FE-ROLE-001.fix: Model all backend roles, preserve role sets, and derive permissions/navigation from the full role/permission payload.

FE-ATT-API.title: Attendance API types do not match backend response contracts
FE-ATT-API.problem: `getSession` is typed as one session while backend returns a list; submit expects `{ success, count }` while backend returns `{ sessionId, created, skippedAlreadyMarked }`; query uses `subjectOfferingId` while backend filter uses `subjectId`; shortage/correction types also differ.
FE-ATT-API.fix: Generate or share API contracts and test against actual controller responses.

FE-STUDENT-001.title: Student gender and portfolio enums do not match backend
FE-STUDENT-001.problem: Frontend uses values such as `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`, `PUBLICATION`, `INTERNSHIP`, and `COMPETITION`; backend uses `UNDISCLOSED` and only CERTIFICATION/PROJECT/ACHIEVEMENT.
FE-STUDENT-001.fix: Align enums or implement explicit mappings.

FE-EXAM-API.title: Exam frontend status types do not match backend
FE-EXAM-API.problem: Frontend types include statuses such as CONDUCTED/RESULTS_PENDING/PUBLISHED while backend returns SCHEDULED/ONGOING/COMPLETED/CANCELLED.
FE-EXAM-API.fix: Preserve backend statuses and map labels separately.

FE-PLAC-API.title: Placement application/interview enums do not match backend
FE-PLAC-API.problem: Frontend uses `INTERVIEWING` and `IN_PERSON`; backend uses `INTERVIEW` and `ONSITE`.

FE-SCH-API.title: Scholarship types do not match backend
FE-SCH-API.problem: Frontend includes MERIT/NEED_BASED/SPORTS/MINORITY/INSTITUTIONAL; backend only accepts GOVERNMENT/COLLEGE/PRIVATE.
FE-SCH-API.fix: Align types or add backend support for the intended categories.

FE-CAMPUS-API.title: Notice model shape mismatch
FE-CAMPUS-API.problem: Frontend expects `published` boolean and attachment objects; backend returns `publishedAt` and `attachmentKeys`.
FE-CAMPUS-API.fix: Normalize backend response in one adapter and expose signed download URLs for attachments.

FE-NOTIF-001.title: `unread=false` query can be transformed to true
FE-NOTIF-001.problem: The same JavaScript Boolean conversion used in the exam DTO is unsafe for query strings; `Boolean("false")` is true.
FE-NOTIF-001.fix: Use explicit string parsing and add tests for both `"true"` and `"false"`.

FE-NOTIF-002.title: Notification enqueue failure can stop fan-out to later recipients
FE-NOTIF-002.problem: Queue insertion is inside the same try/catch around the recipient loop. A queue error can abort the loop after only some users were processed.
FE-NOTIF-002.fix: Persist all in-app notifications first, then enqueue each dispatch independently with per-recipient error handling/outbox retries.

FE-DASH-001.title: Teacher “today's classes” is not based on today's timetable
FE-DASH-001.problem: The helper maps the teacher's subject offerings rather than filtering timetable slots for the current day/time.
FE-DASH-001.fix: Query the timetable for today's date and filter by active validity windows.

FE-DOC-DATA.title: Student document metadata uses fabricated fallbacks
FE-DOC-DATA.problem: Adapter expects fields such as `fileSize`/`fileType` while backend returns `sizeBytes`/`mimeType`, then fills generic values and a fixed academic-year fallback.
FE-DOC-DATA.fix: Map actual backend fields and show unknown metadata as unavailable.

FE-NOTIF-DATA.title: Notification API hides errors as an empty notification list
FE-NOTIF-DATA.problem: Errors are caught and converted to `[]`.
FE-NOTIF-DATA.fix: Preserve the error state and show an explicit retry/error message.  ## G. Operational and deployment findings

DEP-001.title: Vercel mode disables background workers and scheduled jobs
DEP-001.problem: Worker auto-run and scheduler startup are disabled when `VERCEL` is set. The serverless handler only boots the API app. The repository does not provide a separate worker entrypoint/command that a Vercel-only deployment automatically runs.
DEP-001.fix: Deploy a separate long-running worker/scheduler service (Docker/EC2/Render/etc.) against the same Redis and database, or replace the queue with a serverless-compatible job provider. Verify every processor has a live consumer.

DEP-002.title: Vercel API handler does not attach the WebSocket adapter
DEP-002.problem: The normal Nest bootstrap attaches the Socket.IO adapter; the Vercel handler does not. Vercel functions also do not provide a persistent Socket.IO server.
DEP-002.fix: Host the WebSocket gateway on a persistent service or use a managed realtime provider.

DEP-003.title: Local storage default is unsafe for serverless production
DEP-003.problem: Example configuration defaults to `STORAGE_DRIVER=local` and `./uploads-dev`. Production validation does not require S3/R2. Serverless filesystems are ephemeral and often read-only outside temporary paths.
DEP-003.fix: Require S3/R2-compatible durable storage in production and validate its credentials/bucket at startup.

DEP-004.title: Local ports, CORS origins, and rewrite target disagree
DEP-004.problem: Next dev defaults to port 3000; backend example also uses port 3000; Next rewrite fallback points to localhost:4000; CORS example allows 5173 and 3001 but not 3000; frontend example points to a deployed API URL.
DEP-004.fix: Document one canonical local topology (for example backend 3000, frontend 3001, CORS 3001, rewrite/API URL 3000) and make scripts/examples consistent.

DEP-005.title: Prisma deploy script does not run database hardening SQL
DEP-005.problem: `prisma:deploy` runs only `prisma migrate deploy`; `db:setup` additionally runs `db:harden`. The generated `contentTsv` column, GIN/HNSW indexes, and append-only audit triggers are created by the separate hardening script. There is only one tracked Prisma migration file.
DEP-005.fix: Make hardening a tracked migration or make every deployment path run `db:setup`; add a post-deploy assertion for the generated column/index/triggers.

DEP-006.title: Production email configuration is not validated
DEP-006.problem: `SMTP_URL` is optional and no production startup validation ensures email delivery is configured.
DEP-006.fix: Require a working email provider in production or explicitly disable flows that depend on it.

DEP-007.title: Redis client does not recover after exhausting its retry strategy
DEP-007.problem: The retry strategy stops reconnecting after the configured retry attempt; `isHealthy()` returns the stored false state and does not initiate a reconnect.
DEP-007.fix: Use a bounded reconnect/backoff strategy with a health probe that can re-establish the connection, and test outage/recovery.

DEP-008.title: Raw webhook body handling may fail on the Vercel adapter
DEP-008.problem: The serverless adapter registers `express.json()` before Nest initialization. Payment webhook verification relies on raw request bytes and falls back to JSON reserialization when `rawBody` is absent. Re-serialized JSON is not guaranteed to match the provider's signed bytes.
DEP-008.fix: Capture raw bytes before JSON parsing and test a real signed webhook through the deployed adapter.  ## H. Database design and test coverage

DB-001.title: Tenant-owned relations are not protected by tenant-aware foreign keys
DB-001.problem: Many models carry `collegeId`, but relations reference only a globally unique `id`, not `(collegeId, id)`. The application must enforce every cross-table tenant relationship itself; several paths do not.
DB-001.fix: Add composite unique keys and tenant-aware composite foreign keys where feasible, plus service-level validation.

DB-002.title: StudentFee lacks a unique student/fee-structure key
DB-002.problem: There is no unique constraint on `(studentId, feeStructureId)`.
DB-002.fix: Add the unique constraint after cleaning existing duplicates.

DB-003.title: Several workflows rely on application-only uniqueness/concurrency checks
DB-003.status: Confirmed schema gap; impact varies by workflow
DB-003.problem: Timetable overlap, one pending attendance correction, one direct conversation per user pair, and notification idempotency are not enforced by database constraints.
DB-003.fix: Add exclusion/partial unique constraints or idempotency keys and make writes atomic.

DB-004.title: Nullable unique keys permit duplicate global identities/roles in PostgreSQL
DB-004.problem: `User` and `Role` use unique constraints containing nullable `collegeId`. PostgreSQL's normal unique semantics allow multiple rows where the nullable component is NULL.
DB-004.fix: Use partial unique indexes for global rows or `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` where supported, and make bootstrap creation atomic.

DB-005.title: RAG vector dimension is fixed at 1536 while config is variable
DB-005.status: Configuration risk; provider-specific runtime verification required
DB-005.problem: Database column is `vector(1536)`, but `AI_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` is configurable. The OpenAI-compatible provider only sends the `dimensions` request field for OpenAI.
DB-005.fix: Enforce exactly 1536 for this schema or implement a controlled dimension migration/model-specific adapter and validate returned vectors before persistence.

TEST-001.title: Security E2E suite is conditional
TEST-001.problem: Database-backed security tests are skipped unless `E2E_DB=1`.
TEST-001.fix: Run the security suite in CI against an ephemeral PostgreSQL database and make it a required check.

TEST-002.title: Frontend has no browser E2E suite
TEST-002.problem: The frontend has four test files (18 tests in the checked-in report) and no Playwright/Cypress browser workflow.
TEST-002.fix: Add Playwright coverage for login, student attendance/complaints, assignment upload/submission, fee payment, HOD queue, document upload/download, and staff role journeys.

TEST-003.title: Frontend contract tests use mocks rather than the actual backend
TEST-003.problem: Tests validate hand-authored mocked payloads, not responses from the real Nest controllers/DTOs. Several mismatches in this register are therefore not detected.
TEST-003.fix: Generate OpenAPI types and add contract tests against a running backend or schema snapshots.

TEST-004.title: Runtime/build/test claims were not independently reproduced in this audit
TEST-004.problem: Repository documentation reports 27 backend suites / 156 tests and 4 frontend files / 18 tests passing, but this audit did not run those commands.
TEST-004.fix: Run `npm ci`, Prisma generation, backend tests, frontend tests, builds, migrations, and E2E workflows in a real environment; attach logs and commit SHA to the audit.
